raw_case_text: A 54-year-old female was referred to our department with blurred vision and metamorphopsia in her left eye following the diagnosis of DF 2 weeks earlier. She presented all classic systemic symptoms of DF with a papular rash over her arms and hands followed by fever, headache, retro-orbital pain and myalgia. A systemic workup revealed a thrombocytopenia, and a real-time PCR for the dengue virus type 2 was positive, confirming the diagnosis of DF. Noteworthy, she reported 2 previous episodes of DF in 2009 and 2011. Her best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 20/20 in the right eye and 20/150 in the left eye. An anterior segment examination showed no abnormalities. Ophthalmoscopy revealed subretinal fluid and focal hemorrhage in the macula of the left eye (fig. 1a). A fluorescein angiography (FA) showed a hyperfluorescent lesion with well-defined borders and active leakage consistent with classic CNV (fig. 1b). A spectral domain OCT [SD-OCT; Spectralis OCTTM (Heidelberg Engineering, Heidelberg, Germany)] revealed subretinal fluid and focal hyperreflective material in the subretinal space as well as an area with small retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) detachments (fig. 1c). The patient was referred to receive 3 monthly intravitreal injections of ranibizumab (Lucentis; Novartis, Basel, Switzerland, and Genentech, Inc., South San Francisco, Calif., USA). After this loading dose, her BCVA improved to 20/25 in the left eye, and there also was a marked anatomical improvement (fig. 1d). After 6 months, her BCVA was still 20/25 in the left eye and the SD-OCT remained without any signs of active CNV. Two years later, the patient again presented to our service complaining about a reduced VA in her left eye. The BCVA was 20/30 and the FA showed a leaking lesion temporal to and another site of leakage inferior to the fovea. Indocyanine green angiography revealed focal hot spots in these areas (fig. 2a, b). SD-OCT showed marked subretinal fluid, an increased extension of RPE detachments and RPE discontinuity, discrete intraretinal cysts and hyperreflective subretinal material (fig. 2c). The patient underwent 2 monthly intravitreal injections of ranibizumab with functional and anatomical improvement. The BCVA improved to 20/25, but there was persistence of fibrovascular RPE detachment (fig. 2d). Six months later, her VA had returned to 20/20 and OCT showed an absence of disease activity. Regular follow-up visits were recommended.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 54-year-old female presenting with blurred vision and metamorphopsia in her left eye 2 weeks following an acute febrile illness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two weeks prior to presentation, the patient had an acute febrile episode characterized by a papular rash over her arms and hands, followed by fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgias, and thrombocytopenia. Two weeks after this systemic illness, she developed blurred vision and metamorphopsia in her left eye. Two years later, she experienced a recurrent decrease in visual acuity in the same eye.
subjective.past_medical_history: Documented history of two prior episodes of acute febrile illness in 2009 and 2011.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for left eye visual blurring, metamorphopsia, and preceding fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgias, and papular rash. Medications and allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA): 20/20 in the right eye, 20/150 in the left eye. Anterior segment examination: Unremarkable bilaterally. Ophthalmoscopy: Left eye showed subretinal fluid and focal macular hemorrhage. Follow-up at 2-year recurrence: Left eye BCVA was 20/30.
objective.routine_investigations: Systemic laboratory evaluation during preceding acute illness: Documented thrombocytopenia.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial presentation: Fluorescein angiography (FA) showed a hyperfluorescent macular lesion with well-defined borders and active leakage consistent with classic choroidal neovascularization (CNV). Spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT): Subretinal fluid, focal hyperreflective material in the subretinal space, and small retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) detachments. At 2-year recurrence: FA showed active leakage temporal and inferior to the fovea; Indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) showed focal hyperfluorescent hot spots; SD-OCT showed marked subretinal fluid, extensive RPE detachments with RPE discontinuity, discrete intraretinal cysts, and hyperreflective subretinal material.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Classic choroidal neovascularization (CNV) with macular subretinal hemorrhage in the left eye secondary to tertiary dengue virus infection. Diagnostic confirmation: Real-time RT-PCR positive for dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2) during the acute febrile illness; documented history of confirmed dengue episodes in 2009 and 2011. Multimodal retinal imaging (FA, ICGA, SD-OCT) confirmed active CNV.
Plan & Outcome: Initial episode treated with a loading regimen of 3 monthly intravitreal injections of ranibizumab (Lucentis), resulting in BCVA improvement to 20/25 in the left eye and anatomical CNV resolution on SD-OCT at 6 months. Recurrence at 2 years was treated with 2 monthly intravitreal ranibizumab injections, achieving BCVA improvement to 20/25 and full restoration to 20/20 at 6 months with complete resolution of subretinal fluid and quiescent disease.
